geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the cantilever-only top gesture into a split-wing composition so the mass can open toward the access edge and form a meaningful void.
Split along the long axis to preserve the compact bar logic while creating a usable central/public threshold.
Keep the two parts connected so the gesture remains one coherent building rather than two unrelated fragments.
Introduce a grounded spine to mark entry and strengthen the active street edge required by the program.
Size the spine as a slender public seam rather than a second main block.
Keep the ground response low enough to read as an open, accessible public edge under the main mass.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the current one-piece cantilever emphasis with a split-wing / ground-spine logic so the street edge can open into a legible public threshold rather than remaining a sealed compact object.
Enable a connective bridge condition after the split so the dominant mass remains continuous while creating a usable void beneath or between parts.
Add a grounded public spine to strengthen the access-edge response and preserve neighborhood-active frontage.
Keep the ground spine present but slender so it reads as an entry/public seam rather than another block.
Limit the spine height to maintain a clear public opening and avoid re-sealing the base.

rationale: The candidate reads consistently across all four views as one bent slab with a small cantilever, so it is not fragmented and the silhouette is coherent. The main issue is semantic: the mass is too self-contained and sealed at the ground, with only a weak seam relative to the verified access edge and no convincing public void, court, or active threshold. For neighborhood living / mixed-use, the form needs a stronger ground response and clearer hierarchy between occupiable base and calmer upper mass. The current section also feels generic rather than program-led; it resembles a compact sculpted object more than a street-oriented neighborhood building. The stepped/bent roof is acceptable as a variation, but it does not by itself establish the required public relationship or usable void logic.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much lower and simpler than the candidate; mostly single-story pavilion language, so do not copy its scale or volumetry.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact street-facing mass with a clear public threshold and a small attached vertical/service element; useful as a precedent for active ground edge and canopy logic.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Larger and more urbanized than the candidate; candidate should borrow the threshold logic, not the overall midrise massing.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Attached streetwall composition with offset volumes and a readable setback between masses; supports mixed-use hierarchy and active edge.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Too expansive and sectional for this compact brief; the candidate should not drift into a long-looped or waterfront-civic typology.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/courtyard-bearing continuous massing can support neighborhood living when the void is programmatically legible and the ground edge stays active.

warnings: Parcel containment appears satisfied in the visible views, but the access-edge response is weak.
The dominant gesture is coherent, but the ground plane does not yet read as publicly usable.
Avoid pushing this toward a tower or large-span typology; the brief is neighborhood living.
